question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Galileo Galilei and Simon Marius each independently spotted Jupiter's four biggest moons--Io, Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto--and 391 years later, in 2001, astronomers located another Jovian moon, named Eurydome. ______ scientists have identified eighty moons circling Jupiter.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'To date,' logically frames the current count of eighty moons as the running total reached over time.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Certain biologists favor the biological species concept (Mayr 1942), while others rely on the unified species concept (Queiroz 2007), and at least fourteen additional concepts circulate throughout the field. Yet this absence of agreement shouldn't necessarily worry anyone. Those who back a pluralist rather than a single, monistic approach to defining a species ______ that a range of species concepts suits the equally varied ways the term is applied across the discipline.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The plural subject 'Those' requires the plural present-tense verb 'argue.'

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Modernista architects of the 1800s celebrated the natural world in their work. Admittedly, the rippling exterior wall and plant-like window trim of Torre Cortes--a private residence designed in the Modernista style by Salvador Valeri i Pupurull--could never actually sprout in a forest. ______ Valeri i Pupurull's fondness for curves over right angles and his flourishes drawn from plants and animals still reveal nature's influence.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Still,' signals the concession that nature's influence remains visible despite the house not literally growing.

question: According to the text, what attracts divers and scientists to blue holes such as the Far Side Blue Hole and the Taam Ja' Blue Hole? Blue holes--large marine sinkholes such as the Far Side Blue Hole in the Abaco Islands--usually form where the ocean floor consists of dissolvable rock like gypsum, since erosion of that rock is essential to their creation. The fossils preserved inside blue holes draw many divers and scientists to them. At present, the deepest blue hole ever recorded is the Taam Ja' Blue Hole in Chetumal Bay, Mexico, which Joan A. Sanchez-Sanchez and colleagues measured at no less than 420 meters below sea level.
option a: A desire to watch the rock inside the blue holes erode
option b: A hope of observing the fossils preserved within the blue holes
option c: An interest in comparing how deep the Far Side Blue Hole and the Taam Ja' Blue Hole are relative to other blue holes
option d: A commitment to safeguarding the gypsum and other dissolvable materials in the blue holes
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text states the preserved fossils are what draw divers and scientists to blue holes.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? Betty Smith's 1943 novel A Tree Grows in Brooklyn is frequently called autobiographical. The label fits--the life of the book's protagonist, Francie Nolan, echoes Smith's own in many ways--but it shouldn't be read as implying that every character or incident in A Tree Grows in Brooklyn corresponds to something real. A great deal of the book is entirely invented, so readers who ignore this and dwell too heavily on the overlaps between the story and Smith's life may thus ______
option a: portray A Tree Grows in Brooklyn as having a larger readership than it truly has.
option b: give too much weight to how much Smith borrowed from writers who came before her.
option c: deny that Smith used real-world material when composing A Tree Grows in Brooklyn.
option d: overlook just how much inventiveness Smith displays in the novel.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Fixating on real-life parallels causes readers to miss the extensive invention Smith brought to the book.

question: Which choice most logically completes the text? The English professional soccer club Arsenal Football Club, whose home kit is predominantly red, won more than half of its home fixtures between 1947 and 2003--a larger share of home games than Hull City Association Football Club, whose home kit is not red, managed over the same span. In a study, Martin J. Attrill and colleagues noted that the color red can provoke fear and hesitation in people, which they believed helped account for Arsenal's record. However, when Nadav Goldschmied and colleagues re-examined that study's published figures, they found no sign that teams in red are any likelier to win than others, indicating that Arsenal's red kit ______
option a: worsened the play of the teams Arsenal faced.
option b: had no bearing on how satisfied fans were with Arsenal's play.
option c: made Arsenal's players more anxious than they would have been in a different color.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The reanalysis finding no red-team win advantage implies the red kit gave Arsenal no real edge.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? Averaging 59.4 degrees Fahrenheit in summer, Stockholm is a European ______ many travelers recommend, particularly between June and September.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The restrictive clause 'that many travelers recommend' takes no comma and correctly uses 'that.'

question: The student wants to identify who wrote the Arya-Siddhanta. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: Aryabhata (476-550 CE) was an Indian astronomer and mathematician. He wrote the Arya-Siddhanta. The Arya-Siddhanta is a work on ancient Hindu astronomy. The text has been lost. It survives only because other writers have referred to it.
option a: The Arya-Siddhanta is a work on ancient Hindu astronomy.
option b: An Indian astronomer and mathematician who lived from 476 to 550 CE wrote a text that is now lost.
option c: The Arya-Siddhanta was written by Aryabhata, an Indian astronomer and mathematician.
option d: The Arya-Siddhanta is a lost text.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice names both the text and its author, Aryabhata, answering who wrote it.

question: Which quotation from a researcher's publication would most effectively support the student's claim? A student is writing an essay about cultured meat--meat grown in a lab that is meant to reduce the number of livestock slaughtered for food. The student wants to argue that producing cultured meat could prove useful in responding to an anticipated broad shift in the public's behavior.
option a: "The flavor of meat from livestock differs across species (from pig to chicken to cow), and is also influenced by farming conditions and the breeds and genders of animals."
option b: "Consumers tend to believe that using less packaging when selling meat products in stores would have a significant effect on the environment."
option c: "A growing population that is including significantly more meat in its diet will contribute to an increasing demand for meat products in the 21st century."
option d: "Researchers who advocate for the development of lab-grown meat claim that it's better than conventional meat because its nutritional content can be adjusted."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A population eating far more meat is the widespread behavioral change cultured meat could help address.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Beatrice, a wind farm sited off the coast of Scotland, generates roughly 588 megawatts (MW) of electricity a year. ______ Hornsea Project One, an English offshore wind farm that is the highest-producing single offshore farm anywhere, yields 1,218 MW of electricity.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'By comparison,' fits the contrast between Beatrice's output and Hornsea's much larger output.

question:
Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
Reported Annual Travel Distances in Four Studies of Migrating Animal Populations
Species | Continent | Distance (km) | Measurement method
Blue wildebeest | Africa | 650 | RTD
Elk | North America | 1,200 | GPS
Gray wolf | Asia | 7,247 | GPS
Caribou | North America | 1,250 | RTD
Some researchers gauge how far migrating animals travel each year by fitting them with GPS tracking collars. Others record annual round-trip distance (RTD), defined as twice the distance between the two habitats a population moves between each year. One researcher contends that because GPS logs every movement an animal makes, tracking a population by GPS would produce far larger recorded travel distances than the RTD method would. For instance, it's quite likely that the distance reported for the ______
option a: gray wolf would be greater than 1,200 kilometers if the RTD method had been used.
option b: blue wildebeest would be greater than 7,247 kilometers if the GPS method had been used.
option c: gray wolf would be less than 7,247 kilometers if the RTD method had been used.
option d: blue wildebeest would be less than 650 kilometers if the GPS method had been used.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Since RTD yields lower distances than GPS, the gray wolf's GPS figure of 7,247 km would be smaller under RTD.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? To write the entry for "arroyo"--a word for the bed of a stream or creek that runs dry from time to time--the editors of Home Ground: A Guide to the American Landscape enlisted nonfiction writer Arturo Longoria. For "lek," however, they turned to the ______ author of The Very Rich Hours.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No comma follows 'poet,' and a comma after the name sets off the appositive 'author of The Very Rich Hours.'

question: The student wants to point out one or more regions where purple loosestrife is causing environmental or economic harm. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal? While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes: A nonnative species counts as invasive when it inflicts environmental or economic damage on an ecosystem. Purple loosestrife is a wetland plant originally from parts of Eurasia. It also grows in the northern and western US, where it outcompetes native plants and depletes aquatic nutrients. In the US it is regarded as an invasive species.
option a: Purple loosestrife is native to the northern and western US, but elsewhere it causes environmental or economic harm.
option b: Purple loosestrife can be found in the northern and western US, where it crowds out native plants and reduces aquatic nutrients.
option c: Purple loosestrife is considered invasive because it crowds out native plants and reduces aquatic nutrients, causing environmental harm.
option d: Purple loosestrife, a wetland plant native to parts of Eurasia, is considered an invasive species.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Only this choice names the region (northern and western US) where the plant does its documented harm.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "good" most nearly mean? The following text is from Charles Chesnutt's 1905 novel The Colonel's Dream. Mr. French and Mr. Kirby are business partners.
Seated across from Kirby was Mr. French, the senior partner and the older of the two--one might reasonably have placed his age somewhere in the disputed range between forty and fifty. Even from his seated figure his good height was apparent, and he held the upper part of his body erect with the effortless ease one tends to associate with military training.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Good height' here means a considerable or substantial height.

question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text as a whole? Films adapted from popular books frequently do well commercially: when the two widely read novels How to Train Your Dragon and Brooklyn were turned into motion pictures, people flocked to theaters to see them. To investigate whether adapting a book into a film also affects the book's popularity, researchers gathered figures from online platforms about The Monuments Men and two other books that had been adapted for the screen. They found that each film's release date coincided with a rise in interest in the corresponding book.
option a: It provides specific examples that support the claim made earlier in the sentence.
option b: It points out that a general rule mentioned earlier in the sentence has some exceptions.
option c: It sets up a contrast between two artistic forms that is further explored in the next two sentences.
option d: It states a common belief that is disproved by the research findings detailed in the next two sentences.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The underlined clause gives two concrete film examples backing the claim that book-based movies succeed commercially.

question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English? In 2022, Carnegie Hall's digital Timeline of African American Music was ______ input from Maureen Mahon, Michael Veal, and other leading scholars--to weave together text and music clips, thereby inviting users to hear genres such as ragtime and funk as well as read about them.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No punctuation belongs between 'redesigned' and 'with,' which introduce a single continuous phrase.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? The Hornbostel-Sachs system groups musical instruments according to how they produce sound. The alphorn, for instance, an instrument popular in Switzerland, generates its sound mainly through air vibrating within the instrument's body. ______ under the Hornbostel-Sachs system, the alphorn is classified as an aerophone.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Thus,' draws the conclusion that follows from the alphorn producing sound through vibrating air.

question:
As used in the text, what does the word "delicate" most nearly mean? The following text is adapted from Kenneth Grahame's 1908 novel The Wind in the Willows. The Mole, having gotten lost in the woods, has just been found by a friend. Snow is beginning to fall.
The wood that had so terrified the Mole now looked altogether different to him. Holes, hollows, pools, pitfalls, and the other dangers facing a traveler were disappearing fast, and a shining carpet was rising up on every side--one that seemed too delicate for rough feet to tread upon.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The fresh snow carpet is described as delicate, meaning fragile or easily damaged.

question:
Which choice best states the main idea of the text? The following text is adapted from Matthew Arnold's 1869 nonfiction book Culture and Anarchy.
Replying to some foreign criticism of how the English abroad dress, look, and behave, The Times [a British newspaper] insists that the English ideal is for everyone to be free to act and appear exactly as he pleases. Culture, however, works tirelessly not to let whatever a crude person happens to like become the standard by which he shapes himself, but instead to move ever closer to a real sense of what is beautiful, graceful, and becoming--and to bring the crude person to like that.
option a: The English are not as well known for their sense of taste as they ought to be.
option b: Most people disagree with each other on what is beautiful.
option c: Culture's duty is to use scientific methods to determine what is beautiful.
option d: One of the functions of culture is to create a consensus about matters of good taste.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Arnold's central point is that culture works to build shared agreement about what is beautiful and in good taste.

question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition? Researchers in France say that leopards and brown bears rank among the twenty most "charismatic" animals (defined as "attractive, fascinating, or appealing"). To build their top-twenty list, the researchers drew on survey data from Western Europe. Europeans' feelings about leopards and brown bears might not be shared elsewhere in the world, ______
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: 'Of course' fits the acknowledgment that a Europe-based list may naturally not reflect global attitudes.
